notes: EBIT is modeled as an EBIT proxy: income before income taxes plus interest expense, net (used because an 'Operating income' / 'EBIT' line item is not explicitly labeled as such in the financial statement excerpt). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001701605/000170160526000007/bkr-20251231.htm))

DA equals 'Depreciation and amortization' from the cash flow statement; capex equals 'Expenditures for capital assets' (absolute value). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001701605/000170160526000007/bkr-20251231.htm))

NWC definition used for historical: (Total current assets - Cash and cash equivalents) - (Total current liabilities - short-term and current portion of long-term debt). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001701605/000170160526000007/bkr-20251231.htm))

2026 revenue in the base case is anchored to company FY2026 guidance ($27.25 billion) from 4Q25 prepared remarks, then followed by modeled growth rates for 2027-2030. ([investors.bakerhughes.com](https://investors.bakerhughes.com/files/doc_financials/2025/Q4/Baker-Hughes-4Q25-Earnings-Call-Prepared-Remarks-1-25-2025.pdf))

EBIT margin, D&A%, capex%, and NWC% for forecast years are base-case modeling assumptions (not direct company guidance). Management references margin/cost initiatives and targets for Adjusted EBITDA margin, used directionally as context. ([investors.bakerhughes.com](https://investors.bakerhughes.com/files/doc_financials/2025/Q4/Baker-Hughes-4Q25-Earnings-Call-Prepared-Remarks-1-25-2025.pdf))

NOL balance sourced from 2025 Form 10-K note on NOL carryforwards; NOL utilization percent is an explicit modeling assumption set to 0.80. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001701605/000170160526000007/bkr-20251231.htm))

Investments and preferred equity are set to null/0 because the schema requires a valuation-mapping convention that is not unambiguously specified in the supplied primary excerpts; noncontrolling interests are included from the balance sheet. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001701605/000170160526000007/bkr-20251231.htm))

Peer comps are filled using an external NTM snapshot that explicitly indicates it is illustrative; refresh these inputs with your preferred market-data terminal before final valuation outputs. ([mergersandacquisitions.net](https://mergersandacquisitions.net/insights/oil-gas-services-m-a-trends-analysis-report))

catalysts: Regulatory clearance and closing of the Chart acquisition, followed by Day-1 integration execution and synergy realization. ([investors.bakerhughes.com](https://investors.bakerhughes.com/files/doc_financials/2025/Q4/Baker-Hughes-4Q25-Earnings-Call-Prepared-Remarks-1-25-2025.pdf))

Sustained IET order intake (power systems/LNG momentum) translating into higher backlog conversion and improved mix/cash generation. ([investors.bakerhughes.com](https://investors.bakerhughes.com/files/doc_financials/2025/Q4/Baker-Hughes-4Q25-Earnings-Call-Prepared-Remarks-1-25-2025.pdf))

Further margin progress from productivity and cost-out initiatives (company commentary targets higher Adjusted EBITDA margin by 2028). ([investors.bakerhughes.com](https://investors.bakerhughes.com/files/doc_financials/2025/Q4/Baker-Hughes-4Q25-Earnings-Call-Prepared-Remarks-1-25-2025.pdf))
company_overview: Baker Hughes is an energy technology company serving the energy and industrial value chain, organized into Oilfield Services & Equipment (OFSE) and Industrial & Energy Technology (IET). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001701605/000170160526000007/bkr-20251231.htm))

The business combines project-based and longer-duration technology/service revenue streams, with IET positioned to capture power systems, LNG, and other energy infrastructure end-markets. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001701605/000170160526000007/bkr-20251231.htm))
current_context: FY2026 guidance (starting point for the base-case): company anticipates 2026 revenue of $27.25 billion and Adjusted EBITDA of $4.85 billion, with effective tax rate projected to fall within 22% to 26%. ([investors.bakerhughes.com](https://investors.bakerhughes.com/files/doc_financials/2025/Q4/Baker-Hughes-4Q25-Earnings-Call-Prepared-Remarks-1-25-2025.pdf))

Management highlighted IET order momentum, including record IET orders and backlog visibility, and noted strong working-capital performance in Q4 2025 supported by collections and customer down payments. ([investors.bakerhughes.com](https://investors.bakerhughes.com/files/doc_financials/2025/Q4/Baker-Hughes-4Q25-Earnings-Call-Prepared-Remarks-1-25-2025.pdf))

Chart acquisition: management expects closing in the second quarter (timing subject to regulatory progress). ([investors.bakerhughes.com](https://investors.bakerhughes.com/files/doc_financials/2025/Q4/Baker-Hughes-4Q25-Earnings-Call-Prepared-Remarks-1-25-2025.pdf))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue starts from FY2026 guidance and then steps to modest growth, reflecting normalization after 2025 while IET order durability supports upside visibility. ([investors.bakerhughes.com](https://investors.bakerhughes.com/files/doc_financials/2025/Q4/Baker-Hughes-4Q25-Earnings-Call-Prepared-Remarks-1-25-2025.pdf))

EBIT margin is modeled to gradually expand from ~2025 levels toward a low- to mid-teens steady state, consistent with management’s cost-out and margin expansion emphasis through the near term and beyond. ([investors.bakerhughes.com](https://investors.bakerhughes.com/files/doc_financials/2025/Q4/Baker-Hughes-4Q25-Earnings-Call-Prepared-Remarks-1-25-2025.pdf))

Capital intensity is kept broadly stable (~mid-4% of sales) to reflect ongoing investment needs, while working-capital intensity normalizes from an elevated 2025 level toward a more typical run-rate for long-cycle services. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001701605/000170160526000007/bkr-20251231.htm))

Balance-sheet adjustments for valuation use cash and total debt from the latest annual report, with noncontrolling interests incorporated from the equity section. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001701605/000170160526000007/bkr-20251231.htm))
key_risks: Cyclicality in OFSE and broader upstream/downstream capex environment could pressure volumes and pricing, offsetting IET gains. ([investors.bakerhughes.com](https://investors.bakerhughes.com/news/press-releases/news-details/2026/Baker-Hughes-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx))

Working-capital volatility (progress collections/deferred income dynamics) can change free-cash-flow conversion relative to the DCF build. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001701605/000170160526000007/bkr-20251231.htm))

Execution and regulatory timing risk around the Chart acquisition may affect near-term reported results and leverage targets. ([investors.bakerhughes.com](https://investors.bakerhughes.com/files/doc_financials/2025/Q4/Baker-Hughes-4Q25-Earnings-Call-Prepared-Remarks-1-25-2025.pdf))
Tax-rate normalization and NOL utilization assumptions could differ from model expectations. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001701605/000170160526000007/bkr-20251231.htm))

valuation_summary: The DCF uses an EBIT-based operating cash flow build (EBIT proxy, plus D&A, less cash capex, less the change in NWC), with a Gordon-growth terminal value. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001701605/000170160526000007/bkr-20251231.htm))

A WACC in the 8% range is applied as a sober discount-rate assumption for an industrial/service business; terminal growth is set at 2% as a long-run nominal proxy. ([mergersandacquisitions.net](https://mergersandacquisitions.net/insights/oil-gas-services-m-a-trends-analysis-report))

Oilfield-services and energy-technology peer multiples (NTM snapshot) are used only as a cross-check; they should be refreshed with live data before investment committee use. ([mergersandacquisitions.net](https://mergersandacquisitions.net/insights/oil-gas-services-m-a-trends-analysis-report))
